title: Chapter 114
content:
"Wait here," Lan Wangji told Wei Wuxian.

"Are you sure you don't want me to come in with you?"

Lan Wangji shook his head. "If you go inside, he will only be more furious."

Wei Wuxian considered it. Fair point. Lan Qiren looked like a candle flickering in a gale every time he laid eyes on him, clutching his chest and wheezing harder than usual. Better to show a little mercy and spare the old man the headache.

Lan Wangji lingered, looking as though he wanted to say something, but Wei Wuxian cut in before he could start. "Alright, alright, I get it. No running, no loud noises, no this, no that, right? Relax! Since I'm back with you, I'll be on my absolute best behavior. I won't break a single rule on that Wall of Discipline. Well... I'll try."

Without missing a beat, Lan Wangji replied, "It is fine. Even if you do—"

Wei Wuxian’s ears perked up instantly. "Hm?"

Lan Wangji seemed to realize just what had slipped past his lips. He looked away for a beat, turning back only once his expression had settled into its usual deadpan gravity. "...It is nothing."

Wei Wuxian feigned innocence, blinking up at him. "Come on, what were you going to say? Even if I break them, what?"

Lan Wangji knew damn well he was playing dumb. Keeping his face completely blank, he repeated, "Wait for me out here."

Wei Wuxian waved a hand dismissively. "Fine, fine, I'll wait. Don't be so grumpy. I'm going to go play with your bunnies."

Leaving Lan Wangji to face the storm of Lan Qiren's spit-flying lecture on his own, Wei Wuxian was dragged off at breakneck speed by Little Apple. Ever since they stepped foot into the Cloud Recesses, the beast seemed charged with chaotic energy, possessed by the stubborn strength of an ox. Wei Wuxian couldn't hold the reins to save his life, and the stubborn donkey hauled him clean across the grounds straight to a lush, rolling patch of grass.

Scattered peacefully across the meadow were over a hundred chubby, snow-white fur-balls. Little pink three-petaled noses twitched in unison, their long, translucent ears occasionally fluttering in the breeze. Little Apple strutted forward with its snout held high, wedging itself right into the thick of them as if staking out prime real estate.

Wei Wuxian dropped into a crouch, scooping up a random rabbit and idly scratching its belly. Were there really this many last time I was here? he wondered. Is this one a boy or a girl? Huh... boy.

That train of thought suddenly made him realize: in all this time, he’d never actually checked whether Little Apple was a lady or a gent. He glanced over his shoulder to inspect, but before he could get a clear look, rustling behind him caught his attention. He spun around.

A petite girl stood clutching a small woven basket, hesitating over whether she should approach. Catching Wei Wuxian whipping his head around to stare, she froze like a deer in headlights, a violent blush rushing straight up to her hairline.

She was clad in the standard Gusu Lan uniform, her forehead ribbon tied impeccably straight across her brow.

Wei Wuxian's jaw nearly hit the turf. Well, look at that! A real, live one in the wild!

A female cultivator. An actual female cultivator from the Gusu Lan Clan.

The Gusu Lan Clan was legendary for its rigid prudishness. The age-old doctrine of absolute segregation between men and women was drilled into the disciples’ heads from the cradle like an endless Buddhist chant. The living and training quarters for male and female disciples were partitioned with militant precision; stepping over that line was entirely out of the question. Even night-hunts were divided down the middle—either an all-male squad or an all-female squad, with co-ed missions practically unheard of. It bordered on tyrannical.

Back when Wei Wuxian studied in the Cloud Recesses as a teenager, he had never laid eyes on a single girl, leading him to harbor deep suspicions that Gusu Lan female cultivators were an urban myth. Once or twice, he’d caught the faint sound of girls reciting texts from afar. But the second curiosity got the better of him and he tried sneaking over to investigate, the sharp-eyed patrols would catch him instantly and drag Lan Wangji over to play warden. After a few failed attempts, his enthusiasm burned out and he dropped the matter entirely.

And now, here he was, face-to-face with a living, breathing female Lan disciple inside the Cloud Recesses for the very first time. Alive! A real girl!

Wei Wuxian straightened his spine, his eyes lighting up. Just as he took a step forward, Little Apple sprang to life, practically shoving him aside with its flank to trot straight up to the girl.

Huh?

The donkey sidled up to her, ducked its head obediently, and practically shoved its snout and fuzzy ears right under her hand for a scratch.

Huh? What?

Face flaming, the girl stared at Wei Wuxian in an awkward daze, clearly at a total loss for words. Wei Wuxian squinted, a prickle of familiarity tugging at his memory. It clicked a second later—wasn't she that round-faced girl he’d crossed paths with on the road right after slipping out of the Mo Estate, the one he’d briefly run into again at Mount Dafan?

Wei Wuxian had never met a stranger he couldn't chat up with a grin and a few shameless jokes, let alone an acquaintance with a good head on her shoulders. He gave her a cheerful wave. "Hey, it's you!"

The girl clearly remembered him too—both the soot-stained version and the cleaned-up face standing before her. She fidgeted awkwardly for a moment, her hands twisting the handle of her basket as she mumbled, "Yes... it's me..."

Tossing aside the rabbit he’d just thoroughly inspected, Wei Wuxian tucked his hands behind his back and strolled over, peering into her basket of carrots and fresh greens. "Here to feed the bunnies?"

She gave a small nod. Since Lan Wangji was off handling his uncle, Wei Wuxian was bored out of his mind and looking for amusement. "Need a hand?"

Unsure of what else to do, the girl nodded again. Wei Wuxian pulled out a fresh carrot, and the two of them crouched down together in the clover. Little Apple promptly plunged its snout into the basket, rooting around for an apple; finding none, it grudgingly clamped its teeth around a carrot to chew on instead.

The carrots were remarkably crisp. Wei Wuxian casually snapped off a bite for himself before offering the rest to the nearest rabbit. "Do you always come out here to feed them?"

"No..." she stammered softly. "I only started recently. When Hanguang-jun is here, he takes care of them himself. If he's away, Young Master Lan Sizhui and the others look after them. And if none of them are around, we step in to help..."

Wei Wuxian couldn't help the mental image forming: Lan Zhan feeding rabbits? How young was he when he started keeping them? Did he carry a cute little woven basket around just like this?

Quickly swatting the dangerously adorable mental image out of his head, Wei Wuxian asked, "So you're an official disciple of the Gusu Lan Clan now?"

"Mn," she replied shyly.

"Gusu Lan is a good place," Wei Wuxian mused. "When did you join up?"

Gently stroking the plush back of a white rabbit, she murmured, "Not long after Mount Dafan..."

Just then, the soft crunch of boots pressing into the turf broke through the quiet. Wei Wuxian glanced over his shoulder. Right on cue, Lan Wangji was striding toward them across the meadow.

The girl scrambled into a fluster, instantly bounding to her feet and offering a picture-perfect, deeply reverent bow. "Hanguang-jun."

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod in return.

Wei Wuxian stayed right where he was on the grass, looking up with a lazy grin. The poor girl looked terrified out of her wits—not that anyone could blame her; disciples her age were universally terrified of Lan Wangji. Gathering her skirts, she panicked and took off like a startled deer.

Wei Wuxian called after her retreating figure, "Hey, wait! Little sister, you forgot your basket! Hey! Little Apple! Get back here! Why the hell are you running after her?! Little Apple!"

Neither the girl nor the donkey paid him the slightest bit of attention.

Left with only a few carrots rolling around in the bottom of the basket, Wei Wuxian looked up at Lan Wangji, sighing, "Look what you did, Lan Zhan. You scared her off."

If Lan Wangji had truly wanted to keep his approach silent, would either of them have heard a single footstep?

Flashing a cheeky grin, Wei Wuxian held up a fresh carrot toward him. "Want some? You feed the rabbits, I'll feed you."

Lan Wangji looked down at him with an unreadable, stoic gaze. "Get up."

Wei Wuxian tossed the carrot over his shoulder, holding up a single, limp hand with dramatic laziness. "Pull me up."

Lan Wangji hesitated for a split second before reaching down to take his hand. The instant their fingers locked, Wei Wuxian yanked hard, dragging him straight down into the clover.

With their territory invaded by two chaotic giants, the rabbits panicked, scurrying in frantic circles around the tangled bodies. A few that were especially fond of Lan Wangji actually reared up on their hind legs and leaned against him, seemingly distressed that their master had suddenly dropped dead.

Lan Wangji shooed them aside with practiced, gentle patience, his voice steady as ever. "Cloud Recesses, Wall of Discipline, Rule Seven: Do not harass female cultivators."

Wei Wuxian countered smoothly, "You said it didn't matter if I broke the rules."

"I did not."

"Oh, come on. Just because you didn't finish the sentence means it doesn't count? Whatever happened to Hanguang-jun's golden word?"

Lan Wangji gave him a flat look. "'Every day.'"

Wei Wuxian reached up, patting his cheek with exaggerated pity. "Did your uncle chew you out just now? Come on, spill. Let gege pamper you a little."

Lan Wangji didn't bother calling out the laughably clumsy topic change. "He did not."

"Really? Nothing at all? Then what did he say to you?"

Lan Wangji quietly wrapped an arm around his waist, keeping him close. "Nothing much. It has been long since everyone gathered. He is holding a family banquet tomorrow."

Wei Wuxian laughed. "A banquet? Sure, sure, I'll be on my absolute best behavior. Won't embarrass you for a second." Then, his smile softened as his mind drifted to Lan Xichen. "How is your brother?"

A brief silence fell between them. "I will visit him later."

Zewu-jun had spent the last few months locked away in secluded meditation; Lan Wangji was bound to have a long, heart-to-heart talk with him sooner or later. Wei Wuxian shifted his weight, looping an arm around Lan Wangji's back to give him a comforting, rhythmic pat.

After a quiet moment, he added, "Now that you mention it, where are Sizhui and the kids? Usually, they'd be swarming around us at the gates, chattering up a storm."

Hearing him bring up the boys, the tension in Lan Wangji's brow eased slightly. "I will take you to them."

When he led Wei Wuxian over to find Lan Sizhui, Lan Jingyi, and the rest of the juniors, the teenagers barely managed a few muffled whimpers of joy before freezing dead in place. It wasn't that they didn't want to jump up and greet them—they physically couldn't.

A dozen boys were lined up in a neat, trembling row beneath the covered walkway, doing handstands. Each of them had stripped off their heavy outer robes, clad only in thin white under-tunics. Upside down, their feet pressed straight into the air, with sheets of paper and an inkstone set out on the floor before them. Left hands braced against the wooden planks for balance, their right hands gripped calligraphy brushes, painstakingly scratching dense, black characters across the page.

To keep their forehead ribbons from dragging on the ground, every single boy had the tails clamped tightly between his teeth, drenched in cold sweat and completely barred from speaking. What had sounded like "excited greetings" were just a chorus of muffled, wide-eyed grunts of muffled joy.

Taking in the line of violently shaking, precarious silhouettes, Wei Wuxian winced. "Why does it have to be a handstand?"

"Punishment," Lan Wangji replied plainly.

"I know it's a punishment! I can see what they're copying—it's the Gusu Lan Clan Rules. I've got the Conduct and Etiquette section memorized backwards and forwards by now. What did they do to earn this?"

Lan Wangji’s tone was cool and measured. "Failing to return to the Cloud Recesses by the designated deadline."

"Ah."

"Night-hunting in the company of the Ghost General."

Wei Wuxian grinned. "Well now! You kids sure have guts."

"A third offense," Lan Wangji added.

Wei Wuxian rubbed his chin, thinking that if that was the case, it was no wonder the upright and unyielding Lan Qiren had dropped the hammer on them. Truth be told, copying rules in a handstand was practically getting off with a slap on the wrist.

Lan Wangji paced slowly down the line of trembling boys, giving their work a brief inspection. Halting before one of them, he said flatly, "Your calligraphy. It lacks discipline."

The poor boy, still biting down on the tails of his forehead ribbon, choked out a tearful, muffled rasp: "Y-yes, Hanguang-jun. I will start this page over."

The rest of the juniors who hadn't been singled out breathed a collective, silent sigh of relief—they’d passed inspection.

As the two of them stepped away from the veranda, the memory of his own miserable days spent copying rules washed over Wei Wuxian with sudden sympathy. "Just keeping that pose is hard enough. If you made me write while doing a handstand, I wouldn't get down a single stroke. Heck, my handwriting isn't even neat when I'm sitting down!"

Lan Wangji glanced his way. "That is true."

Wei Wuxian knew he was thinking back to the long days spent supervising his punishments in the Library Pavilion. Chuckling, he asked, "Did you have to do handstands when you got punished as a kid, too?"

"Never," Lan Wangji replied.

Right, obviously, Wei Wuxian thought. Lan Wangji had been the poster child of the great clans since he was in diapers; every move he made was measured to the millimeter like it had been drawn with a ruler. When would he have ever stepped out of line? And if he never broke a rule, why would he ever get punished?

Wei Wuxian grinned. "Here I was thinking that ridiculous arm strength of yours was forged through sheer suffering."

"I was not punished," Lan Wangji clarified. "Yet it was indeed forged this way."

Wei Wuxian blinked, surprised. "If you weren't being punished, why on earth were you doing handstands for fun?"

Keeping his eyes locked straight ahead, Lan Wangji murmured, "It calms the mind."

Wei Wuxian leaned in close to his ear, his voice lilting with a wicked, playful purr: "And just what was troubling the icy, untouchable Hanguang-jun's mind so much that he needed to calm down?"

Lan Wangji looked at him, maintaining a stoic silence.

Basking in his victory, Wei Wuxian smirked. "So if you've been building that arm strength since you were little, does that mean you can do pretty much anything while doing a handstand?"

"Mn."

Seeing his lashes dip low, his answer carrying a faint, subtle edge of bashfulness, Wei Wuxian completely lost all filter. Leaning in, he whispered, "Can you fuck me upside down, too?"

Lan Wangji met his gaze evenly. "We can try."

Wei Wuxian burst into wild laughter. "Hahah—wait, what did you just say?"

Lan Wangji looked him dead in the eye. "We will try it tonight."

Wei Wuxian, for once, was speechless.
